{
  "hypothesis": "Predicted that the giving and taking frames would have asymmetric and opposing effects on male and female dictators' allocations and social types, with males becoming more selfish and females becoming more egalitarian in the taking frame compared to the giving frame.",
  "design": "between, with two treatments (Giving game vs. Taking game) and a balanced pool of male and female participants",
  "manipulation_or_predictor": "Dictator game framing (Giving frame where the dictator decides how much of an additional £10 to transfer to the recipient vs. Taking frame where the recipient has access to an additional £10 and the dictator decides how much to transfer to themselves) combined with dictator gender",
  "outcome_measure": "Amount allocated to the recipient (amount given in the giving game or £10 minus the amount taken in the taking game), and categorical dictator types (selfish vs. egalitarian)",
  "population_and_setting": "Students at the University of East Anglia participating in a computerized laboratory experiment",
  "sample_size_total": 280,
  "recruitment_and_incentive": "Recruited randomly through the online recruitment system ORSEE with a £3 show-up fee plus earnings from the dictator game",
  "analysis_plan": "Mann-Whitney tests, OLS regressions, and Probit models predicting allocations and dictator types based on treatment, gender, their interactions, and age",
  "preregistered_or_confirmatory": "not stated",
  "other_methods_notes": "Sessions involved 70 dictators and 70 recipients per treatment, maintaining gender balance (35 male and 35 female dictators per treatment). Roles were passive for recipients in the first part."
}
